lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
State the rule and next two terms: 15, 12, 9, 6…

FEEDBACK
Subtract 3 each time; next 3, then 0.

WATCH FOR
Guessing the next term without a consistent rule invents a false pattern.

For twelve sequences, write the rule and the next three terms. Mark additive vs multiplicative for six.

Write a short reflection naming one step you corrected and why.

lesson.parent_notes:
Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: For twelve sequences, write the rule and the next three terms. Mark additive vs multiplicative for six. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Written model 1: Sample: new numbers solved with visible working for pattern; key places/values named. Do not award marks for retyping the model.

Parent: Written model 2: Sample misconception: Guessing the next term without a consistent rule invents a false pattern.. Correction uses Subtract 3 each time; next 3, then 0.. Why: restores accurate pattern.

Parent: Likely misconception: Guessing the next term without a consistent rule invents a false pattern. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

Parent: Short-answer focus 1: Solve one fresh problem that uses pattern with different numbers from the worked model. Show working and name the places or values that matter.

Parent: Short-answer focus 2: Describe one likely mistake with pattern, show corrected working, and say why the correction works.

Parent: Marking notes: Accept any mathematically valid solution that uses new numbers, shows working for pattern, and names places/values. Reject copied model numbers. / Accept a named misconception about pattern, corrected working, and a method reason. Reject vague “I was wrong” with no repair..

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
Sequence 4, 7, 10, 13… rule +3. Term after 13 is 16. Multiplicative: 2, 6, 18… ×3 each time.

TRY FIRST
State the rule and next two terms: 15, 12, 9, 6…

FEEDBACK
Subtract 3 each time; next 3, then 0.
teach_steps.explain:
Number patterns follow a rule that generates each next term; describing the rule lets you continue and check the sequence.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner choose methods based on place value, quantity and accurate working, rather than guessing digits by shape alone. Keep every step justified.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the places, values or distances that carry the method. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Compare your working with the feedback: did you use the same skill and show your reasoning? If a digit or place is uncertain, identify what would have to be regrouped or counted again. One deliberate, justified revision is more useful than writing a longer answer.
teach_steps.notice: Guessing the next term without a consistent rule invents a false pattern. Correct the value or method, not just the appearance of the digits.
